On-Chain Operator. Lesson 12.4, Treasury and the liquidity ladder. Navy and cyan. One idea at a time. You write it down. Education only.
You already keep a journal and a kill rule. A balance sheet is that habit turned into accounts.
Banks match the timing of assets to the timing of what they owe.
Size (example: $5,000/month spend) T0 Instant.
Blue-chip stablecoin lending, split across 2 protocols.
PTs maturing on dates you'll need the money (Lesson 10.1).
Next 6–12 months of planned spending T3 Growth.
The rest, within caps Refill downward on a schedule: T1 tops up T0 monthly; maturing PTs top up T1.
Never fund a T0 need by selling a T3 position in a bad market.

On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: T2 maturities matched to planned spending. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Monthly refill schedule set. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: T3 never used for day-to-day needs. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
Check yourself. 1. Why hold T0 in plain stablecoins earning little? The answer: Instant, certain access. It's the tier that pays today's bills without selling anything.
Check yourself. 2. What's T2 for? The answer: Known future spending, with maturities matched to when the money is needed and a fixed return locked in.
Check yourself. 3. What does the ladder prevent? The answer: Forced selling of growth positions at bad prices to meet short-term needs.
By the end of this lesson, you'll be able to structure reserves so money is available when it's needed, earning a return at every tier.
Your ladder: Refill downward on a schedule: T1 tops up T0 monthly; maturing PTs top up T1.
T0 Instant, Seconds, Stablecoins in the operating wallet, 1 month: $5,000.
T1 Same day, Hours, Blue-chip stablecoin lending, split across 2 protocols, 5 months: $25,000.
T2 Term, Scheduled, PTs maturing on dates you'll need the money (Lesson 10.1), Next 6 to 12 months of planned spending.
T3 Growth, Days to weeks, Strategy positions, L.P.s, staking, The rest, within caps.
Let's look at the diagram: The liquidity ladder.
It's everything we've just said, in one picture.
T0 $5,000 + T1 $25,000 equals 6 months instantly available.
T2 holds three PTs maturing in 3, 6 and 9 months, each sized for 3 months of spending.
A minus 50% market day touches none of it.
First, T0 + T1 at least 6 months of obligations.
And finally, T3 never used for day-to-day needs.
